_comment: The county report contract for scripts/site_profile.py. Hand-edited; no process writes it. Adapted from pricephillips/data-center-map templates/manifest.json (section order) and configs/definitions.json (terms defined on first use). 'sections' is the report's section order; an optional section is left out when it has nothing to show. A term's definition prints in parentheses the first time the term is used and the bare term afterwards. Definitions and notices carry no digits, so every digit in a report traces to a record read at run time. Local reports have no section of their own: each prints inside the section it concerns, and a county with none says nothing about them. The readings (How this county compares, Diffusion from adjacent counties, Comparable decided projects, Activity nearby) carry data-center-map's way of reading a county without its model: counts, dates and distances only.

sections.heading: Activity nearby in the last two years

restriction_instrument.definition: a local or state law that materially constrains wind, solar or battery storage: a moratorium, a ban, a setback, a height, noise or size limit, or a district where the use is prohibited; one instrument may cover several technologies and is counted once

severity.definition: a score from one to four: one for procedural friction, two for a material burden, three for a likely de facto ban, four for an explicit moratorium or ban; the rule that set each score is printed beside it

verification.definition: how a record stands under the evidence standard: verified when the instrument, or the minutes that adopted it, was read; located when a primary source is attached but was seen only as search-index text; not verified when only a news article or a compiled tracker is behind it

contested_project.definition: a project-level opposition event, such as a hearing, a permit denial, a campaign or a cancellation, with an outcome on the shared ladder of blocked, restricted, advanced or pending; an outcome is confirmed only by independent evidence and is otherwise shown as unverified

negative_check.definition: a reviewed record that someone searched the county's codes, minutes and news for a restriction and found none; its evidence grade runs from A, when independent kinds of source were read, to D, and it goes stale after a year

pending_candidate.definition: a row in the review queue that no reviewer has decided on; it is shown for context and is never published

siting_standard.definition: one feature of a local wind or solar ordinance as NREL compiled it, such as a setback, a height limit or a prohibited district, labelled unverified until a reviewer checks it against the ordinance

local_report.definition: what a local contact, a meeting someone attended or a document someone saw says about the county; recorded outside the repository, never verified and never published

data_center_event.definition: a government action on data centers recorded by the data-center-map platform for the same county or a neighbor; context only, never counted as a renewable restriction

reference_group.definition: a set of counties a county is read against: every county in the frame, or the counties of its own state, where siting law is set; counts of counties, never rates

diffusion_reading.definition: where a county sits on a fixed ladder of reasons to look next door, from a neighbor that enacted recently while this county holds an unresolved record, through a cluster of restricting neighbors, to a single neighbor with an old instrument; a pattern to check, not a prediction

comparable_decided_project.definition: a contested project within a hundred miles of the site or in the same state whose outcome is terminal on the ladder, blocked, advanced or restricted, shown with the mechanism behind it and with unverified outcomes labelled as recorded

notices.descriptive: This report describes what the records hold. It does not say what caused any decision, it scores nothing, and it does not predict the outcome of any project.
notices.empty: An empty section means nothing is recorded, not that nothing happened, unless a negative check says that someone looked.
notices.evidence: Every record line names its source and how it was seen. A news article or a compiled tracker locates an instrument but does not verify it; only the instrument or the minutes that adopted it do.
notices.selection: The records exist because an ordinance, a fight or a lawsuit was visible enough to be compiled; projects that proceeded without a recorded fight and quiet counties are absent by construction, so every count is a floor and no figure here is a rate of opposition.
notices.limits: Severity is a rule applied to the instrument's own terms, not a graded intensity. NREL's siting standards were compiled with language models and are unverified until a reviewer reads the ordinance. A record without coordinates is placed at its county's centroid. Cases are only those linked to the records shown. Nothing here is scored, weighted or modelled.
